BLOCKER: `Scan` still appends every page into one `objects []datastore.ObjectInfo` slice and then builds a full `map`; pagination gains nothing — the entire listing is still materialised, directly violating the "never materialises the full listing" acceptance criterion (only `MaxObjects` bounds it).

`LocalStore.ListPage` calls `s.List(ctx, prefix)` and sorts the whole set — it materialises the full listing on every page request (O(n·pages) I/O), so the local implementation does not satisfy the memory-bounded contract it claims to implement.

`objectURL` takes `tenant` from a query parameter and injects it via `objpolicy.WithTenant`, so any admin caller can mint URLs for an arbitrary tenant; the AC requires the *authenticated* tenant context. This is a tenant-boundary bypass waiting to be relied upon.

No tests were added for the CLI report/exit codes (0/1/2) or for the `/admin/objects/url` route validation, which the AC explicitly requires ("Tests cover pagination, shard locks, CLI report/exit codes and the URL route validation"). Shard-lock and pagination tests are present; the other two are missing.
MAJOR: `objreconcile` library module now depends on `objstore` + `s3store` (pulling minio, crypto, compress etc.) solely for `cmd/objreconcile`. This couples a pure reconciliation library to storage adapters and bloats every consumer's dependency graph; the command should live in its own module.

`S3Store.ListPage` returns as soon as `limit` is reached without cancelling/draining the minio `ListObjects` channel — the producer goroutine blocks on send until the context ends (CLI uses `context.Background()`, so it leaks for process lifetime).

Page size `1000` and the `MaxObjects` bound are magic numbers inline in `Scan`; no named constants, no metrics/logs around pages fetched or bound violations — poor observability for a drift job that will run long-lived.

`objectURL` silently ignores invalid/negative `ttl_seconds` and accepts any `method` string (including PUT) without an allowlist; AC cites "URL route validation", which is currently neither strict nor tested.
`objpolicy.Mint` errors are returned verbatim via `err.Error()` as a 400 body — internal/provider details leak to API clients.
MINOR: CLI reads the entire manifest with `os.ReadFile` and unmarshals twice into `entries`/`wrapped`; a large manifest re-introduces the unbounded-memory pattern this change is meant to eliminate (stream decode or single-pass shape detection).
CLI has no signal handling/`context.WithCancel`, so an in-flight S3 scan cannot be gracefully interrupted.

No compile-time interface assertions (`var _ datastore.PrefixLister = (*LocalStore)(nil)` / `(*S3Store)(nil)`), so a refactor silently drops a store out of the paginated path and falls back to full `List` with no test failing at build time.
Paginated path lacks tests for `MaxObjects` overrun, `ListPage` error propagation, and `limit`/empty-page termination edge cases.

`keyShards` FNV shard index has no test asserting bounded lock count under many distinct keys (the AC asks for shard-lock coverage; the existing test only exercises behaviour, not the fixed-pool property).
NIT: Error message inconsistency between paginated and legacy paths ("more than %d objects" vs "%d objects exceed the scan bound (%d)").

`keyShards` and retained `mu` field naming/formatting drift in `LocalStore`; `sort.Slice` on every local page allocates comparators repeatedly — `sort.Strings`-style precomputed order would be cheaper.
`wrapped` struct is allocated per call and could be a package-level type for reuse/clarity.
SUMMARY: The direction (optional `PrefixLister`, shard-pool locks, real CLI + admin route) is right, but the memory-bounded guarantee is not actually delivered — pages are still concatenated into a full in-memory slice and `LocalStore.ListPage` just wraps a full `List`. The signed-URL route derives tenant from a caller-supplied query parameter rather than the authenticated context, and the AC-mandated CLI/URL tests are absent. Fix the streaming/bound semantics and tenant sourcing, split the CLI module, then add the missing tests before this ships.
